🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO FILES 20 COMPLAINTS OVER 17 MIGRANTS DEAD IN ICE CUSTODY</u>

Foreign Secretary Roberto Velasco Álvarez says Mexico is following up on 17 cases of Mexican nationals who died during ICE operations or in ICE custody — and has filed 20 formal complaints with US authorities to establish the circumstances of each death: eight with state prosecutors and twelve with district attorneys in Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Louisiana, Missouri and other states. Not a press release — case-by-case legal pressure, on US soil.
banner: MEXICO FILES 20 COMPLAINTS OVER ICE DEATHS

🔥🇲🇽 <u>VERACRUZ AUDITS ALL 260 PUBLIC NOTARIES OVER PROPERTY-THEFT CASES</u>

Governor Rocío Nahle's administration is auditing every one of the 260 notaries public operating in Veracruz, after a string of property-dispossession cases against Veracruz families became public in recent months. Nahle warned she will not tolerate illegal acts that put families' patrimony at risk. Notaries are where despojo gets its paperwork — auditing all 260 is what actually going after land theft looks like.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>SHEINBAUM: PRI'S VIOLENT TANTRUMS ARE A COLLAPSING PARTY'S DESPAIR</u>

President Sheinbaum says the PRI's recent episodes of physical and verbal violence reflect the "frustration" and "desperation" of a party that keeps losing public support — and she called on people not to fall for the provocation. The party that governed Mexico for 71 uninterrupted years now has to scream to be noticed.
banner: SHEINBAUM: PRI RAGES AS SUPPORT SINKS

🔥🇲🇽 <u>FGR RAIDS TABASCO MAYOR'S HOME — MC'S BACA SEVILLA NOW A FUGITIVE</u>

Federal prosecutors raided the home of Alfonso Baca Sevilla, the Movimiento Ciudadano mayor of Paraíso, Tabasco, as part of Operativo Enjambre — a sweep that also hit properties of municipal officials and left several people detained. Local media report the mayor slipped the operation and is now a fugitive, with an apparent arrest warrant over his head. The FGR has not yet said what he is accused of. The opposition's municipal map keeps shrinking — one raid at a time.
banner: TABASCO: MC MAYOR FLEES FGR RAID

text:
🍓🇲🇽 <u>US TAKES AIM AT MEXICAN STRAWBERRIES WITH DUMPING DUTIES</u>

The US Commerce Department set preliminary antidumping margins of 3.37 to 5.28% on Mexican strawberries — a case opened December 31, 2025 at the request of Florida growers.

Mexico's Economy Ministry fired back that Commerce arbitrarily applied "winter strawberry" and "regional market" concepts that the US International Trade Commission had already preliminarily discarded — assumptions inconsistent with the WTO Antidumping Agreement and the USMCA itself.

At stake: nearly 5,000 Mexican producers and 151,000 workers. First tomatoes at 17%, now berries. Some "free trade" partner.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>NOGALES: FENTANYL GOES NORTH, GUNS GO SOUTH</u>

Two sides of the same border, same week. US CBP agents at Nogales found some 9,000 fentanyl pills hidden under a car's floor and 18 kilos of cocaine inside a stove's ventilation system — and in an outbound inspection heading into Mexico, three pistols, magazines and a laser sight.

On the Mexican side, Sonora state police seized over 200 fentanyl pills in the Héroes de Nogales neighborhood, "in a coordinated action with federal authorities."

Washington counts the pills. Mexico keeps counting the guns.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>CFE POWER OUTAGES DOWN 37% UNDER SHEINBAUM</u>

Mexico's public utility keeps quietly delivering: power interruptions fell 37% in January–July versus 2024 — from 433,345 to 273,452 — and customer complaints dropped 10%, the CFE reported.

Average restoration time went from 25 hours to 7, a 72% improvement, after 7.6 million tree-trimming jobs and maintenance on more than 18,000 transformers.

Twenty-seven states improved, led by Chiapas with a 77% reduction.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>HIDALGO DEVELOPMENT POLE ADVANCES WITH 147 BILLION PESOS</u>

Plan Mexico keeps landing. The Zapotlán development pole in Hidalgo is moving forward with 147 billion pesos across 130 projects and 191,000 jobs on the books.

DEWA Capital is putting in 10.1 billion pesos for urbanization and industrial plants; Cooperativa Cruz Azul another 6.5 billion to reactivate the Tula cement plant — 14,200 direct and indirect jobs from those two alone, on a 910-hectare site.

"It's good news for Hidalgo and for the country," President Sheinbaum said.

🇲🇽🐄 <u>SCREWWORM CASE IN SONORA DAYS BEFORE US BORDER REOPENS TO MEXICAN CATTLE</u>

Sonora confirmed its first case of New World screwworm, in Álamos, just days before the USDA reopens the Douglas, Arizona crossing to Mexican cattle on August 24 — the first step in the staged reopening after more than a year of suspension.

Sanitary authorities are holding a containment cordon. Before the shutdown, Sonora alone shipped the US about 320,000 head of cattle a year; Mexico aims to close 2026 with 400,000 exported.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>DEA CHIEF PUBLICLY BACKS MEXICO'S SECURITY STRATEGY</u>

The head of the DEA used his stage at the IDEC 2026 conference in Buenos Aires to praise Mexico's Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch as a "trusted partner" and "good friend of the United States," crediting him with nearly two decades of service.

"Secretary Harfuch, friend, thank you for your leadership, your friendship and collaboration. More than 100 countries appreciate you being here," Terry Cole said, in a recording released by Mexico's SSPC.

The agency that spent years treating Mexico as the problem now opens its conference applauding Mexico's security model.
